parsed.rationale: Although both records are `type-alias-object` kinds with `shared_field_count: 2` and no context flags set, they carry distinct names (`PauseWXYC` in `Shared/Intents/Sources/Intents/PauseWXYC.swift` vs. `WhatsPlayingOnWXYC` in `WXYC/iOS/Intents.swift`) that suggest they represent different Siri/App Intents actions — one for pausing playback and one for querying what is currently playing. The structural similarity is almost certainly coincidental: both are thin type-alias wrappers over an Intents framework type, so their shape converges by construction rather than by shared domain logic. Merging or extracting them would conflate two semantically distinct intent actions and break the intent-handler dispatch that depends on their separate identities.
